pyre_field.name: The Pyre Field
pyre_field.description: A field of black stubble on the southern edge of Greyhallow, where the village burns its dead. Seven pyres stand in a crooked row, six of them cold and grey. The seventh, yours, still smoulders, though the flames have the decency not to touch you. Past the edge of the field the Pall hangs like a wall of wet wool, swallowing the road south. The village lies north.
pyre_field.short: Seven pyres in a crooked row, one still smouldering. The Pall walls off the south; the village lies north.
pyre_field.first_visit:
You wake to the smell of your own funeral.

Charred timber shifts beneath your back. Someone laid you out with copper coins on your eyes; they slide off as you sit up and roll into the ash. Your chest aches with a strange, steady warmth. Through a split in your shirt, beneath the breastbone, something glows: a sliver of gold no longer than a fingernail, pulsing slow as a heartbeat.

The fire around you is real. It simply will not burn you.

south.blocked_text: You take three steps into the Pall. The ash closes over your head like water, and you hear, quite clearly, your mother calling your name. Your mother has been dead for nine years. You step back out.

pyre.text: Your pyre. Someone built it with care: cedar for sweetness, pitch for speed. A wreath of dried marigolds lies scorched at its foot. Whoever mourned you meant it.
pyre.take_text: You pull a brand from the pyre. It doesn't burn your hand, which is disquieting, and it goes out at once, which is worse. You drop it.

other_pyres.text: Six cold pyres, six heaps of grey. In two of them the bones are missing entirely, as though whoever burned there got up and walked off before the job was finished. There may be something worth finding if you sift through them.

pall.text: The Pall. Up close it isn't fog at all but ash, too fine to see grain by grain, hanging in the air and slowly turning. Somewhere inside it a dog is barking, and has been barking for a very long time without ever stopping for breath.

chest.text: You press a hand to your breastbone. The sliver of light beneath the skin is warm and does not hurt. When you look north toward the village it brightens a little, as though it wants to go there.

search.text: You rake through the ash of the neighbouring pyres. Most of it is just ash. In the third, your fingers close on a blackened little sunburst on a leather thong, a pilgrim's charm, whole despite the fire.

ambient: A cinder drifts up from your pyre and goes out.
Somewhere in the Pall, the dog keeps barking.
Ash settles on your sleeve. You brush it off. More settles.

village_square.name: Greyhallow Square
village_square.description: Greyhallow's square is a ring of slate-roofed houses around a dry fountain. Most doors are nailed shut; a few have the Dawnfather's sunburst painted on them in hurried yellow, the paint still tacky. In the fountain's basin burns a small, fierce light that no one has fed in days: an Ember Shrine. The chapel steps rise to the north, the Last Candle inn leans in from the east, and the old well squats at the end of a lane to the west. South lies the pyre field.
village_square.short: A ring of shuttered houses around a dry fountain and its Ember Shrine. Chapel north, inn east, well west, pyre field south.

shrine.text: A bowl of bronze set in the dry fountain, holding a flame no bigger than a fist. When you lean close, the sliver in your chest answers it with a pulse of warmth. Resting here feels like being remembered. (Ember Shrines save your progress, and if you fall, you will wake at the last one you touched.)

doors.text: The painted sunbursts are a prayer: Dawnfather, see this house. The nailed doors are a different sort of prayer. Behind one of them, someone is very carefully not breathing.

ambient: A shutter creaks open an inch, then closes again.
Somewhere a child is crying, and someone is telling them softly to hush.
The shrine-flame leans toward you like a sunflower.

village_well.name: The Old Well
village_well.description: West of the square the lane dead-ends at Greyhallow's well, a squat ring of mossy stone under a peaked roof of shingles. The rope hangs slack and frayed; the bucket is gone. A cold breath rises from the shaft, smelling of iron and deep water. Beyond the well, the lane runs a few more yards and then simply stops, eaten by the Pall.
village_well.short: A mossy well with no bucket, at the end of a lane the Pall has eaten.

west.blocked_text: The lane runs into the Pall and does not come out. You can hear the miller's wheel turning somewhere in there, slow and wet, though there is no wind and no water to turn it.

well.text: You lean over the lip. Far, far below, something catches the light from your chest and glints back at you. It could be water, or an eye, or a star.

use.text: You drop a pebble down the shaft and count. You get to eleven before you hear it land, and the sound isn't a splash. It's a small, clear chime, like glass on glass.

rope.text: The rope is frayed through where the bucket hook used to be. Someone cut it, or something chewed it.

ambient: A cold draught sighs up from the well, like the earth exhaling.
Water drips somewhere deep below, very slowly, in no rhythm you can follow.

the_last_candle.name: The Last Candle
the_last_candle.description: The Last Candle is warm the way only places with a fire and too few people can be. Stools sit upturned on the tables; the hearth is banked low. Behind the bar a broad woman polishes a tankard she has probably been polishing since sundown, watching you the way you'd watch a ghost who has walked in and not yet asked for a drink.
the_last_candle.short: The inn's common room: a low hearth, upturned stools, and Marta behind the bar.

hearth.text: Peat and applewood, banked to last the night. The embers brighten a little as you pass, then settle, as though they recognised you and decided not to make a fuss.

tankard.text: The tankard is very clean. It was very clean an hour ago, too.

ambient: The fire pops. Marta does not look up.
A cat you hadn't noticed leaves the room, offended by your existence.

chapel_steps.name: Chapel Steps
chapel_steps.description: Worn steps climb to the Chapel of the Dawn, a squat stone church whose bell-tower has lost its bell. The great doors are chained shut from the outside with a heavy padlock and a hand-painted sign: CLOSED BY ORDER OF THE SYNOD. DO NOT DISTURB THE DROWNED. Beneath it someone has added, in chalk: they disturb US. A lych-gate to the east opens onto the graveyard.
chapel_steps.short: The chained doors of the Chapel of the Dawn. The graveyard lies east through the lych-gate.

variants.description: Worn steps climb to the Chapel of the Dawn, a squat stone church whose bell-tower has lost its bell. The chain lies coiled on the steps where you dropped it, the padlock hanging open. The doors stand ajar on darkness and the smell of standing water. A lych-gate to the east opens onto the graveyard.

north.label: chapel doors
north.blocked_text: The chain holds. The padlock is old, but it is not that old.

padlock.text: A heavy iron padlock stamped with the Synod's sunburst. The keyhole is large and old-fashioned.

variants.text: The padlock hangs open from a link of loose chain.

use.text: You fit the sexton's iron key to the padlock. It grinds, catches, and turns. The chain slithers down the doors and pools on the steps like something shed.

padlock.use_fail: Without the key, the padlock isn't going anywhere.

sign.text: CLOSED BY ORDER OF THE SYNOD. DO NOT DISTURB THE DROWNED. Underneath, in chalk, in a child's careful capitals: they disturb US.

tower.text: The belfry is empty, its beam split. Whatever happened to the bell, it happened violently.

ambient: From behind the chapel doors comes a sound like many people murmuring underwater.
A gust of ash rattles the chain against the doors.

graveyard.name: Greyhallow Graveyard
graveyard.description: Greyhallow's graveyard slopes away from the chapel in uneven terraces, its headstones leaning together like old men sharing a secret. Many of the graves are freshly dug. More than a few have been freshly un-dug, the earth heaped outward as though from below. A sexton's shed sags against the eastern wall, nettles growing waist-high around it.
graveyard.short: Leaning headstones, open graves, and the sexton's shed in its nettles.

variants.append: Behind the shed, a slate has been heaved aside from a stair leading down into the hill.

graves.text: You read the nearest stones. HARL TANNER. BESS TANNER. LITTLE TOM TANNER. All three graves are empty, the soil pushed outward. Someone has stuck a sprig of rosemary into each heap, for remembrance, or as an apology.

abels_grave.text: SEXTON ABEL MORROW. HE KEPT THEM DOWN. The earth here is packed hard and undisturbed. Small mercies.

shed.text: A tool shed, door hanging from one hinge. Inside: spades, a pickaxe, a coil of rope gone to rot, and an old coat on a nail. The nettles behind it have been trampled flat recently, in a single narrow path.

variants.text: The sexton's shed. Behind it, the slate you moved lies against the wall, and a narrow stair descends into the hill.

search.text: You follow the trampled path through the nettles behind the shed. Set flush into the earth is a slab of slate with an iron ring in it. When you heave it aside, cold air sighs up from a stair cut down into the hillside.

ambient: A crow lands on a headstone, considers you, and decides against it.
Something shifts under the soil nearby. Then, thankfully, stops.
The wind turns over a page of an old hymnbook somebody left on a grave.

ossuary.name: Abel's Ossuary
ossuary.description: A low vault lined floor to ceiling with skulls, set in tidy rows like jars in a larder. Abel kept it well: each skull has a name chalked on its brow in a neat, looping hand. A few of the names have been rubbed out from the inside. On a stone shelf, the sexton's candle-stubs stand in a careful row, as though he expected to come back.
ossuary.short: The sexton's vault of chalk-named skulls.

skulls.text: MARGERY. OLD PIKE. THE BAKER'S BOY. AGNES (THE OTHER ONE). Each name chalked with care. On the skulls whose names are smeared, the smears are on the inside of the bone, as though something within had wiped them away.

shelf.text: Seven candle-stubs, burned to the same height, in a row. Abel prayed here, every night, for a long time.

ossuary.first_visit: As you reach the foot of the stair, the sliver in your chest flares and every chalked name on every skull seems, for one long moment, to turn toward you.
ambient: Somewhere in the rows, a skull settles with a small click.
The silence here has a texture, like felt.

chapel_nave.name: The Drowned Nave
chapel_nave.description: Water has risen through the chapel floor and stands ankle-deep, black and perfectly still, mirroring the broken vaulting overhead so that you seem to walk across the roof of a second, drowned church. Pews float askew. At the altar end, a sunburst window lets in a grey, sourceless light. Something has been praying here: the kneeler before the altar is worn bright, and the water around it is warm.
chapel_nave.short: The flooded chapel nave, black water mirroring the vaults.
chapel_nave.first_visit: As you step in, every candle in the nave lights at once, then gutters, as if embarrassed. From somewhere behind the altar, a man's voice says, slurred and weary: "Oh, wonderful. Another miracle."

on_enter.text: (You have reached the end of the Milestone 1 test area. More of Greyhallow awakens in later milestones.)

water.text: In the reflection, the chapel is whole: bell in the tower, candles lit, a congregation in the pews. In the reflection, every one of them is turning to look at you.

altar.text: The kneeler is worn bright as a coin. Someone, or several someones, has knelt here a very long time.

ambient: Ripples cross the water from a direction where nothing is moving.
Behind the altar, someone hiccups, then says "pardon" to nobody.
